newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy banks 1997 net profit up, margins down-study.
newsitem.headline: Italy banks 1997 net profit up, margins down-study.

text.p: The Italian banking system can expect to see net profits of 7.1 trillion lire this year against 5.5 trillion in 1996 with significant ROE growth due to reduced provisions and loan adjustments, research body Prometeia said.
Net profits in 1998 were seen at 6.7 trillion lire, but the outlook was less rosy when operating results were examined, it said in its latest report on the banking sector.
It said interest margins were set to fall two percent this year and 6.5 percent in 1998 and these were not likely to be counterbalanced just by banking services.
In 1997, intermediation margins will be stable despite a 12 percent rise in income from services but will fall six percent in 1998 due to lower profits from securities trading.

Banks will have to act to hold down labour costs, Prometeia said, estimating personnel costs will rise by one percent this year and 0.5 percent in 1998, given an annual reduction in the workforce of at least one percent.
Prometeia forecast a significant slowdown in deposits growth and managed savings and only weak development in client loans which were seen rising 2.9 percent this year and 3.2 percent in 1998.
Net stock of bad loans was seen falling while gross assets were seen growing but to an insufficient extent, the report concluded.
